about: The single list of what a Racing Times script may ask for. Both renderers (show-pixel, show-3d) draw exactly these; validate.py enforces them; script_writer and the newsroom skills read their instructions from here. Add a graphic or shot here AND in both renderers, then flip its status to 'ready'. Characters: bible/. Strict mode (newsroom scripts) requires a kind on every sentence.

text_rules.graphic_text: UPPERCASE ASCII only (the pixel fonts have no accents): SAO PAULO, not São Paulo. Use ' - ' as a separator, not a middle dot.
text_rules.sentences: Any characters. Use {text, say} when TTS may mangle a name: text is the subtitle, say is how to pronounce it.

teams.about: Team codes for graphics. Colours are approximate and used only for accents.

wide.desc: Pixie at the desk with the video wall beside her.
wide.use: Default. Introducing a story, linking between items.

close.desc: Tight on Pixie; the wall is out of frame.
close.use: Emotional beats, opinions, cold-open hook, sign-off. Lower thirds show here.

full.desc: The current graphic fills the screen.
full.use: Whenever a graphic must be read: results tables, headline lists, dates. No lower third, no bugs.

two_shot.desc: Pixie and Byte (paddock reporter) side by side.
two_shot.use: The interview segment, when Byte relays attributed quotes.

id.desc: Unique snake_case id, e.g. lead, formula_e, sign_off.

speaker.desc: Who speaks this segment: pixie (default, studio) or byte (grid). A sentence can override it.

graphic.desc: The graphic on the wall (or full screen) when the segment starts.

graphic_b.desc: A second graphic that replaces the first part-way through.

graphic_b_at.desc: 0-1, fraction of the segment at which graphic_b appears. Required with graphic_b.

shots.desc: [[fraction, shot], ...]; first fraction is 0, fractions increase, each < 1. Fraction = share of the segment's spoken length.

point.desc: true: Pixie turns and points at the wall at the start of the segment. Use when she introduces a graphic on a wide shot.

lower_third.desc: {title, sub} name strap; shows for ~5 s on wide/close shots.

logo.desc: Show logo on a moving checker / gold rings.
logo.use: Cold open, or between halves of the show.

headlines.desc: Title bar plus 1-4 lines that slide in one by one, about 1.5 s apart.
headlines.use: The 'this week' menu after the cold open. One short line per story.

p1.desc: Big position number with a driver's name, a detail line and an optional stat, in the team's colour.
p1.use: Race winner, pole sitter, or any single headline result.

name.note: Full name; the small wall view shows only the surname.

results.desc: Classification table, rows slide in from the right.
results.use: Top-5 of a race or qualifying. Put it on a 'full' shot: it is unreadable on the small wall.

rows.note: [pos, SURNAME, TEAM CODE, gap]; winner's gap is WIN or the race time.

champions.desc: Confetti with a big name and a gold sub-line.

bigword.desc: One huge word over animated diagonal lines, with one or two fact lines.
bigword.use: Any story that has a one-word hook: a new car, a venue, a number.

lines.note: The small wall view shows only the first line.

nextup.desc: 'Next race' card with the event, dates and up to two 'later' teasers.

photo.desc: The story's approved photo across the studio wall, with kicker, headline and photo credit. On the pixel show it fills the wall screen.
photo.use: Any story with approved photos. Use several per story (n=1, 2, 3) across segments, so the wall keeps changing. The credit is added automatically; the photo slowly zooms.

story.note: story id from editor_notes.json; the photo comes from photos/photos.json

n.note: which photo of the story (photos.json 'n'); default 1

quote.desc: A short attributed quote with speaker and source.
quote.use: Byte's interview segment. Real quotes only, under 15 words, from a named press release or series report.

standings.desc: Championship table with points and gap to the leader.

driver.desc: Driver card: name, team, and up to three facts. Typographic, no photo.

briefs.desc: Rapid-fire list: series tag plus one line each, ticking through.

items.note: Start each with the series tag, e.g. 'FE: SHANGHAI DOUBLE-HEADER'.

cast.about: Who can speak. Personalities live in bible/<name>.md. Shot names (wide/close/full) apply to the speaker's own set.

sentence.about: A sentence is a plain string (Pixie, kind 'link' or legacy) or an object with these fields.

text.desc: Subtitle text: exactly what is said.

speaker.desc: Overrides the segment speaker for this line (for banter).

kind.desc: fact = from the edition's sources; opinion = the character's view, no new claims; anecdote = history or a statistic, needs source; link = greetings, hand-offs, claim-free jokes.

source.desc: URL. Required when kind is anecdote (from the anecdote-finder agent).

delivery.desc: How the line is spoken and acted: neutral, warm, excited, serious, deadpan, question, aside. Sets the voice's speed, pitch, loudness and pause, plus the character's brows, nods and head tilt. Vary it: no more than two lines in a row with the same delivery. Sensitive stories: serious or warm only.

desk_display.about: Optional top-level script field: the items the desk screen cycles through (6 s each). Default: title, live from <city>, next = the next two story titles.
